ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based customer due diligence under Law No. 14/2022/QH15 and Decree No. 19/2023/ND-CP: identify and verify all UBOs, including indirect ownership through offshore holding structures; screen all members, managers, UBOs, and authorized representatives against OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, UN Security Council consolidated sanctions lists, EU sanctions, and domestic Vietnamese restricted lists; perform enhanced due diligence for politically exposed persons (PEPs), including family members and close associates; perform adverse-media and watchlist screening; maintain transaction monitoring and suspicious-transaction reporting obligations with the State Bank of Viet Nam Money Laundering Prevention Bureau; retain KYC/UBO records for at least five years after the business relationship ends.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: National Business Registration Portal (Cổng thông tin quốc gia về Đăng ký doanh nghiệp) at https://dangkykinhdoanh.gov.vn
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A Vietnamese enterprise name must be composed of Vietnamese-language letters or digits; if using a foreign name element, it must be transliterated or shown in permitted Latin script as prescribed by Decree No. 01/2021/ND-CP. Names must be distinguishable and not identical or confusingly similar to any existing registered enterprise name in Viet Nam. A separately registered English company name may supplement but cannot replace the Vietnamese statutory name.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Names of state agencies, armed forces, People's Committees, or ministries (e.g., 'Chính phủ', 'Bộ Công an', 'Quân đội', 'Ủy ban nhân dân') without prior ministerial/competent-authority consent
'Việt Nam' or 'Vietnam' in certain name constructions where it implies state ownership or misleading official connection
Names identical to an existing registered enterprise or names deceptively similar to protected well-known enterprise names
Words contrary to Vietnamese historical, cultural, ethical, and national-security standards
Offensive or obscene expressions in Vietnamese or transliterated form
Terms such as 'Ngân hàng', 'Bảo hiểm', 'Luật', 'Kiểm toán', 'Chứng khoán' when the proposed LLC does not hold the relevant statutory license
Names referencing the Sultan, royal, or foreign-governmental institutions without foreign-state authorization
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant receives a written or portal notice stating the ground of refusal. Within 30 days from the date of rejection, the applicant may submit an administrative appeal to the Department of Planning and Investment where the enterprise is registered or to the General Director of the Business Registration Management Department, attaching the original rejection notice, corrected proposed name, distinguishing elements, and legal argument. If the administrative appeal is denied, the applicant may initiate an administrative civil proceeding in the Vietnamese court within the statutory limitation period, or alternatively withdraw the proposed name and immediately re-submit a new clearance request through the National Business Registration Portal. Extensions are not statutorily guaranteed; where a name is provisionally cleared, registration completion is required within the 30-day validity window unless extended by express administrative decision.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office cannot serve as the statutory registered head office of a Vietnamese LLC. The LLC must maintain a physical premise in Viet Nam at which the enterprise receives legal documents, administrative notices, and official inspection. PO-box-only or serviced-office-mail-only arrangements are insufficient. For a virtual-concert and metaverse business, a physical registered address is still required, though ancillary business operations may be conducted remotely using cloud infrastructure.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate risk of approximately 30% to 35% within the first 18 months after incorporation, driven by local enterprise registration compliance checks, tax field inspections, and risk-based AML/CFT supervision of FinTech-adjacent businesses with cryptocurrency payment exposure. The likelihood increases if red flags emerge in UBO disclosure, sanctions screening, or repeated changes in managers.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Consular fee tariff plus embassy processing surcharge, where applicable

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Engaged legal counsel / AML compliance advisor
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for transaction-level AML/UBO legal compliance in Viet Nam

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting Vietnamese-language incorporated LLC Charter (Điều lệ công ty TNHH), including foreign-investor provisions, capital contribution schedule, and virtual-event ticket tokenization business scope

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law on Enterprises No. 59/2020/QH14 (Articles 26–27 on Enterprise Registration Certificate issuance; Articles 47–53 on the single-member limited liability company); Law on Investment No. 61/2020/QH14 (Articles 31, 36 and 37 on Investment Registration Certificate); Decree No. 01/2021/ND-CP on enterprise registration procedures; Decree No. 31/2021/ND-CP on investment procedures; Decree No. 122/2021/ND-CP on fees and charges for enterprise registration; Circular No. 01/2023/TT-BKHDT on registration forms and dossier contents.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Provincial Department of Planning and Investment (DPI) of the province or centrally administered city where the registered office is located; online submission through the National Business Registration Portal (https://dangkykinhdoanh.gov.vn) for the Enterprise Registration Certificate and through the National Investment Registration Portal for the Investment Registration Certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Enterprise Registration (Form A-01/B-01 under Circular 01/2023/TT-BKHDT) together with the Company Charter, submitted in the same dossier as the Application for Investment Registration (Form I-1) and, if applicable, the investment project proposal for the foreign-invested LLC.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Viet Nam imposes no statutory minimum charter capital for a foreign-invested LLC engaged in virtual concert hosting and digital ticket tokenization, and no escrow account is required by general company law. The charter capital must, however, be stated in the charter and subscribed in full by each member; under Article 50(3) of the Law on Enterprises, contributed capital must be brought into the company in full within 90 days after issuance of the Enterprise Registration Certificate unless the charter stipulates a shorter or longer term not exceeding the statutory regime. A foreign investor contributing equity must evidence the contribution through a foreign direct investment capital account opened at a licensed bank in Viet Nam.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD / SOLE-MEMBER RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY NAME] LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY. The undersigned sole member and owner of [Company Name] LLC ("the Company"), by executing this resolution, acting as the corporate seat of authority under Article 49 of the Law on Enterprises, hereby adopts the following corporate decisions. 1. CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION AND STRUCTURE: The charter capital of the Company is fixed at USD [amount], subscribed by the sole member [Investor Name], and shall be contributed as provided in the Company Charter. 2. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION: The registered office of the Company is fixed and adopted at [full street address, City, Province, Viet Nam], which shall serve as the Company's principal administrative seat for legal correspondence and tax registration. 3. OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: [Full Name] is hereby appointed as Chief Executive Officer / General Director and legal representative of the Company, with full authority to execute, file, notarize, and obtain all statutory permits, licenses, and registrations required for the incorporation and lawful operation of the Company in Viet Nam. 4. BANKING AUTHORIZATION: The General Director is expressly authorized to open corporate bank accounts and the foreign direct investment capital account, to appoint authorized signatories, and to instruct counsel and tax agents as necessary. 5. EFFECTIVENESS: This Resolution shall become effective immediately, and the Company shall acquire juridical personality from the date the Enterprise Registration Certificate is issued by the competent Department of Planning and Investment. Dated [date], [place], Viet Nam. [Signature of Sole Member].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Legalization, name clearance and preparatory notarization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public office (và n phòng công chứng) in Vietnam; National Business Registration Portal for name search; consular/legalization office for investor documents.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a pre-filing name search on the National Business Registration Portal to ensure the proposed LLC name does not conflict with existing enterprises or violate the naming restrictions under Article 38 of the Law on Enterprises. Prepare and notarize Vietnamese translations of the foreign investor's certificate of incorporation (or passport) and of the proposed charter. Execute a lease or use-right agreement for the registered office address and obtain the owner's consent document. Where the investor is a corporate body, notarize the resolution authorizing the investment and the financial statements proving capital availability.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation or passport of the foreign investor
Notarized Vietnamese translation of investor identity documents
Financial statement or bank certificate evidencing lawful capital availability
Draft Company Charter
Signed authorization letter appointing the legal representative
Office lease agreement or letter of consent from the owner of the registered address
Business name search result
Power of attorney for the notarization agent (if any)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name search is refused or the notary queries any document, the applicant must submit a corrective statement, obtain a fresh notarial copy or revise the name; an administrative complaint may be filed with the provincial DPI under Article 61 of the Law on Enterprises within 30 days from the refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Investment Registration Certificate approval for foreign-invested LLC
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial Department of Planning and Investment (DPI) via the National Investment Registration Portal or the online one-stop service (Cổng Dịch vụ Công trực tuyến DPI).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the investment registration dossier for the foreign-owned LLC. The DPI verifies the legal status of the investor, the project objectives, capital contribution, and compliance with Vietnam's investment admission conditions. Since ISIC 7110 / virtual-concert and digital-ticketing activities are not on the list of prohibited investment sectors, the project may proceed under the non-conditional investment scope. The DPI must issue a written request for corrections or an Investment Registration Certificate (IRC) within 15 days from the date of a complete and valid dossier.
required_dossiers: Application for Investment Registration (Form I-1)
Foreign investor's legal documents and notarized translations
Investment capital availability evidence
Written investment project proposal (technical description, legal form, scale, market plan, and capital plan)
Company Charter draft in Vietnamese
Office lease documentation
Sole member's resolution to establish the enterprise
Appointment document of the legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DPI issues a request for amendment, the applicant must supplement or revise the dossier within 10 working days from the notification. If the IRC is refused, the investor may file an administrative complaint with the Minister of Planning and Investment or initiate a law-suit at the relevant administrative court under Law No. 66/2015/QH14.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Enterprise Registration Certificate issuance and corporate birth
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial Department of Planning and Investment (DPI) through the National Business Registration Portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After obtaining the Investment Registration Certificate, file the enterprise registration dossier with the DPI. The dossier includes the Application for Enterprise Registration, the Company Charter, the list of members, and the list of legal representatives. The DPI must issue the Enterprise Registration Certificate (ERC) within 3 working days if the dossier is valid. The enterprise automatically obtains business legal personality on the date of issuance; the ERC contains the enterprise code, tax code, registered office, charter capital, members, and legal representative.
required_dossiers: Application for Enterprise Registration (Form A-01, as required by Circular 01/2023/TT-BKHDT)
Company Charter in Vietnamese
List of members of the LLC and their subscribed capital contributions
List of the legal representative of the enterprise
Investment Registration Certificate (copy)
Notarized copies of member identity documents
Registered office lease or use-right documentation
Authorization documents for filing agents, if any
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DPI requests corrections, the applicant must amend and re-submit within 10 working days from the receipt of the written notice. A refusal may be appealed to the Minister of Planning and Investment or challenged before the competent court; the enterprise may also re-file a corrected dossier without prejudice to the 3-working-day mandatory processing period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration governance, seal, tax and capital account activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial Tax Department (Cục Thuế), Service of Justice / police for seal recognition (administrative), and a licensed commercial bank (for capital account).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the ERC is issued, obtain the enterprise seal. The seal design and use are no longer subject to a state registry fee but must be produced by a licensed seal engraver and maintained under the control of the legal representative under Article 43 of the Law on Enterprises. Register payroll and employee social insurance as soon as the first employees are engaged, open the company's operating bank account and the foreign-investment capital account at a licensed bank, and register the tax declaration method. File the first statutory license fee (pai thue mon bé) and any value-added tax declarations in accordance with the Law on Enterprise Income Tax and the Law on Value-Added Tax.
required_dossiers: Enterprise Registration Certificate
Company Charter and Board/Sole-Member Resolutions
Notice of seal specimen and seal use regulations
Company bank account opening forms
Tax registration forms and legal representative identity papers
Capital contribution schedule and bank statements evidencing foreign capital transfer
Employment and social insurance registration forms for employees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax authority or bank rejects any application, the applicant must furnish updated attestations, translated corporate documents, or revised resolutions. If the company misses a statutory tax signature deadline, late-filing penalties are mitigated by filing a voluntary correction before the tax authority issues an investigation notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Sectoral notification and environmental compliance confirmation for virtual service activities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial Department of Planning and Investment; Ministry of Industry and Trade (if conducting e-commerce trading through the platform); Ministry of Information and Communications (if later operating a social-network or content-distribution platform); DONRE (if physical premises later trigger environmental thresholds).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify that the company's admitted business lines are not conditional under existing Vietnamese licensing lists; virtual performance hosting and digital ticket tokenization are not classified as industrial production requiring a manufacturing operating license. If the company operates a customer-facing e-commerce platform as a digital intermediary for ticket sale, submit the online notification to the Ministry of Industry and Trade under Decree No. 52/2013/ND-CP (as amended by Decree No. 85/2021/ND-CP). Confirm the company does not act as a payment service provider; USDC conversion and Stripe transactions are executed through licensed payment intermediaries. Complete fire-safety self-assessment for the head office and workplace-accident risk assessment in accordance with the Labor Code and Decree No. 44/2016/ND-CP.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Enterprise Registration
Investor corporate records
Charter and amended business line list
Office floor plan and fire-safety design documentation
E-commerce notification form, if applicable
Environmental assessment confirmation form (if DONRE requires a preliminary review for the office building)
Occupational safety policy and workplace risk assessment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the competent authority treats the activity as a conditional business line, the company must apply for the precise conditional operating license; failure to obtain one within the prescribed period requires suspension of the affected activity. If an environmental threshold is exceeded due to future server deployment, the company shall immediately fulfil the environmental registration procedure under Decree 08/2022/ND-CP or submit an environmental impact assessment report as instructed by the provincial DONRE.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: None applicable—foreign-invested LLC under ISIC 7110 (virtual performance hosting and digital ticketing) is not an industrial establishment; no industrial manufacturing or processing license is required by the Law on Investment or Decree 31/2021/ND-CP.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No operating or manufacturing permit is applicable for a purely digital event-hosting service. The company may, depending on its order-flow structure, only file a post-registration e-commerce notification with the Ministry of Industry and Trade; it does not require a banking or payment-service licence because payment rails (Stripe and USDC) are operated by licensed payment intermediaries.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MONRE) and the Provincial Department of Natural Resources and Environment (DONRE)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt—full EIA report is not required. The project is a non-manufacturing, non-construction virtual event service with no measurable discharge, emission, or land disturbance. If the registered office occupies only a standard leased commercial/office space, the owner of the building remains responsible for the building's environmental registration; the LLC itself only triggers environmental procedures if it subsequently constructs or operates a physical data center or rehearsal studio.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No production wastewater or VOC-emission thresholds apply to the virtual-concert activity. Should future operations include server hosting infrastructure, the enterprise must comply with QCVN 40:2011/BTNMT (industrial wastewater), QCVN 05:2013/BTNMT (ambient air quality) and Decree 08/2022/ND-CP environmental registration thresholds; hazardous waste, if any, must be declared and handled through licensed waste-treatment enterprises under Law on Environmental Protection 2020.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-prevention and fire-fighting compliance under Decree No. 136/2020/ND-CP is required for the leased head-office premises; the enterprise shall obtain the competent fire-police department's written approval or a written acknowledgement that the office is covered by the building owner's existing fire-safety certificate. Structural-load inspection applies only if the company constructs or installs heavy equipment, which is not expected for a virtual-event ticketing operation. Under the Labor Code No. 45/2019/QH14 and Decree No. 44/2016/ND-CP, the employer must perform a workplace risk assessment, implement occupational safety measures, and arrange annual safety training for employees. No separate civil-defense clearance is required for a metaverse-based virtual concert without physical spectators or premises.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: General Department of Taxation (Tổng cục Thuế) under the Ministry of Finance of Viet Nam; e-Tax Portal for tax administration and filing: thuedientu.gdt.gov.vn; National One-Stop Portal: dichvucong.gdt.gov.vn.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-invested limited liability company is established by registering through the provincial Department of Planning and Investment (DPI), which issues the Enterprise Registration Certificate (ERC). Under the national integrated business-tax registration procedure (Decree 01/2021/ND-CP), the DPI automatically transmits registration data to the General Department of Taxation, and the Tax Identification Number (TIN) is issued ex officio. A foreign supplier without a permanent establishment in Viet Nam (e.g., a metaverse ticket platform selling to Vietnamese consumers) must register on the Foreign Supplier e-Tax Portal at etaxvn.gdt.gov.vn and obtain a dedicated tax code pursuant to the Law on Tax Administration (No. 38/2019/QH14) and Decree 85/2021/ND-CP.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: the LLC is a resident corporate taxpayer subject to Corporate Income Tax (CIT) at the standard 20% rate; no pass-through treatment is available. Territorial scope: resident enterprises are taxed on worldwide income, with double-tax relief for foreign-sourced income; non-resident enterprises are taxed only on Vietnam-source income. Qualifying enterprises located in Export Processing Zones (EPZs), high-tech zones, and economic zones may benefit from Tax_Exempt_Zone incentives, including a preferential CIT rate of 10% for up to 15 years and additional exemption/reduction periods.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Viet Nam does not provide US-style check-the-box elections or OECD hybrid mismatch elections. Available statutory elections are limited to: (i) selection of straight-line depreciation life within prescribed bands for fixed assets; (ii) election by an eligible taxpayer to apply the most favorable CIT incentive when multiple incentive regimes overlap; and (iii) voluntary VAT registration under the credit-invoice method by enterprises whose revenue is below the compulsory VAT threshold. Hybrid mismatch consequences are not recognized, and no corresponding election exists.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under the Law on Value Added Tax (No. 13/2008/QH12, as amended by Law No. 31/2013/QH14 and Law No. 66/2025/QH15)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: VND 1,000,000,000 of annual taxable revenue for domestic enterprises and foreign-invested LLCs (mandatory VAT registration); voluntary registration permitted below the threshold. Foreign non-resident suppliers of digital/electronic services (including virtual event ticketing) are mandated to register through the Foreign Supplier Portal when annual Vietnamese-source revenue exceeds VND 100,000,000.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Viet Nam mandates electronic invoicing (e-invoices) in a standardized XML format (Decree 123/2020/ND-CP and Circular 78/2021/TT-BTC). E-invoices must bear a tax-authority-assigned invoice serial number and code, and the invoice data must be transmitted to the National e-Invoice System (hoadondientu.gdt.gov.vn) within 24 hours of issuance. There is no physical fiscal stamp or real-time transactional clearance, but the system applies pre-issuance validation for invoice codes and export invoices must be cross-referenced with electronic customs declarations on VNACCS/VCIS.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A 0% VAT rate applies to: (i) export goods physically leaving Viet Nam, supported by a customs export declaration; (ii) services provided to foreign organizations or individuals and consumed entirely outside Viet Nam, including virtual performance ticketing supplied to non-resident purchasers where the supplier can evidence the offshore status of the buyer, cross-border payment in foreign currency, and offshore consumption; (iii) goods and services supplied to non-residents or export processing enterprises within EPZs, bonded warehouses, and export-processing zones; and (iv) international transportation services. The taxpayer bears the burden of proof and must retain the full statutory documentation bundle.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (electronic declaration in the VNACCS/VCIS customs system)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical export of goods (not applicable to pure offshore services)
Export sales contract with the foreign buyer
Commercial invoice issued to the foreign counterparty
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) or foreign-currency bank payment confirmation evidencing receipt of proceeds from abroad
Zero-rated e-invoice in the statutory XML format with tax-authority-assigned code
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The tax authorities, together with the Vietnam Customs, cross-validate export declarations, e-invoice data, and foreign-currency remittance records. A zero-rating claim lacking substantive documentation is treated as tax evasion and is subject to clawback of the refunded VAT, late-payment interest of 0.03% per day, and administrative fines of 1 to 3 times the evaded tax amount under Decree 125/2020/ND-CP. Issuance of illegal invoices attracts fines up to VND 20,000,000 per invoice. Tax evasion involving amounts exceeding VND 100,000,000 may trigger criminal prosecution under Article 200 of the Penal Code, with penalties including fines and imprisonment. The inspection/audit look-back period is 5 years, but no time limit applies in cases of fraud or intentional misdeclaration.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Bank of Vietnam (SBV / Ngan hang Nha nuoc Viet Nam) acting through the Foreign Exchange Administration Department (Vu Quan ly ngoai hoi), exercising authority under the Law on the State Bank of Vietnam No. 46/2010/QH12, the Law on Credit Institutions No. 47/2010/QH13 (as amended), the Ordinance on Foreign Exchange No. 28/2005/PL-UBTVQH11 (as amended by Law No. 04/2022/QH15), and implementing instruments including Decree No. 70/2014/ND-CP and Circulars No. 02/2021/TT-NHNN, 05/2021/TT-NHNN and 10/2022/TT-NHNN.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Vietnam maintains a bifurcated convertibility regime: the current account is largely convertible, while the capital account is subject to administrative control. For an ISIC 7110 virtual concert and metaverse ticketing entity, receipts from non-resident customers for digital services, virtual performance licensing and tokenized ticketing constitute current-account service transactions and may be freely credited in foreign currency, provided the underlying commercial documentation (service contract, e-invoice or settlement report from the payment platform, and supporting narrative of service delivery) is presented to the licensed servicing bank. Mandatory capital-account controls apply to (i) equity capital contributions, which must enter through the Foreign Direct Investment Capital Account (DICA / tai khoan von dau tu truc tiep) registered with the SBV via the servicing credit institution; and (ii) profit remittances abroad, which are permitted on an annual or six-monthly basis only after the statutory audit is completed, the corporate income tax (CIT) finalization is filed and no CIT, VAT or social insurance liabilities remain outstanding; the remittance is made through the DICA using balance-of-payments (BOP) code 540030 (repatriation of profit from current-year or retained earnings). Full divestment and residual capital repatriation require SBV-approved liquidation and a Capital Account Settlement Certificate. Profit and service proceeds are freely convertible into foreign currency at the authorized bank's quoted rate, but cryptocurrency, including USDC, is not recognized as a lawful payment instrument or a foreign-exchange conversion channel; the SBV has confirmed under guidance (Official Letter 5747/NHNN-PC and Decree 101/2012/ND-CP as amended by Decree 80/2016/ND-CP) that digital assets are neither legal tender nor accepted settlement currency. Accordingly, USDC-denominated revenue must be liquidated into USD offshore and then remitted to Vietnam via SWIFT, or converted onshore only after an offshore conversion step, in order to preserve lawful convertibility and avoid an unlicensed 'de facto' FX business.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under Circular No. 02/2021/TT-NHNN as amended by Circular No. 10/2022/TT-NHNN, 100% of export proceeds earned by a foreign-invested LLC from the supply of cross-border services (including virtual performance hosting, metaverse ticketing and digital content licensing) must be repatriated to a licensed bank in Vietnam through a foreign currency account (tai khoan ngoai te / FCD) within 90 calendar days of the invoice date or the date of service completion, whichever is earlier. There is no mandatory conversion ratio in force today; the mandatory surrender requirement (historically up to 80%) was abolished, and the entity may freely retain the foreign currency, deposit it, convert it to VND at the SBV-referenced exchange rate band, or use it for lawful authorized payments. The servicing bank must be provided with a transaction schedule and underlying service settlement evidence, and the repatriation obligation extends to all proceeds received through foreign-payment intermediaries (e.g., Stripe or offshore EMI accounts), requiring the entity to instruct such platforms to sweep net settlement balances to the onshore FCD account within the statutory window. Non-compliance attracts administrative sanctions under Decree No. 88/2019/ND-CP, including fines up to VND 300 million for late or non-repatriation, temporary suspension of foreign-exchange activity, and mandatory rectification, with aggravating factors applied where crypto settlement rails are used to bypass the FCD process.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_regulatory_filing_obligatio: The LLC must maintain a single DICA registered with the SBV through its principal bank for all direct investment capital inflows and outbound transfers; any opening of a secondary DICA requires prior written SBV approval. The bank files BOP statistical returns (BOP forms) on behalf of the entity, and the entity is obligated to report quarterly loan, capital contribution and guarantee positions to the servicing bank under the Foreign Exchange Administration Department's data collection scheme. Cryptocurrency treasuries are not reportable as monetary assets and, if held, must be disclosed in the audited financial statements as intangible/other financial assets, triggering bank inquiries and potential classification as higher-risk.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: MEDIUM-LOW for direct offshore digital EMI onboarding; HIGH for bank-partnered Banking-as-a-Service (BaaS) rails. Vietnam does not recognize an offshore digital EMI licence (e.g., FCA-EMI, MAS-Major Payment Institution, Lithuania-EMI) as an authorized payment institution. Under Decree 101/2012/ND-CP (as amended by Decree 80/2016/ND-CP), only SBV-licensed non-bank payment intermediaries (intermediary payment services, to chuc trung gian thanh toan) and licensed credit institutions may legally execute payment transactions for residents. An offshore EMI may legally maintain a treasury account for the Vietnamese LLC only as a foreign intermediary; it cannot open an onshore settlement account or execute VND clearing. Stripe, as an unlicensed foreign acquirer, may onboard the LLC through its Singapore entity for global card acquittance, but the net USD settlement must be wired by MT103 to the onshore FCD account within the 90-day repatriation window; Vietnamese banking compliance will treat the Stripe and Coinbase Commerce settlement balances as the primary source of export proceeds and will demand the corresponding settlement reports. USDC treasury management is legally permissible only if held offshore (in the name of a foreign affiliate) and is not recognized as foreign currency for SBV purposes; direct onshore conversion of USDC into VND is prohibited as an unlicensed foreign-exchange activity and will be treated as a payment-systems violation. Recommended structure: (i) offshore treasury vehicle holds USDC and converts to USD via regulated exchanges (Coinbase, Kraken) after each periodic event; (ii) USD swept SWIFT to onshore Vietcombank FCD; (iii) VND conversion executed onshore at spot. This preserves full legal viability and avoids SBV enforcement action.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is effectively mandatory and cannot be fully replaced by remote onboarding. The legal representative of the foreign-invested LLC (Chairman of the Members' Council or the General Director as registered on the Enterprise Registration Certificate) must personally appear at the selected branch to execute the Specimen Signature Registration Card (the dang ky mau dau) and complete the standard face-to-face interview as mandated by SBV's AML/CFT regulations (Law on Prevention and Combating Money Laundering No. 14/2022/QH15 and Circular No. 09/2023/TT-NHNN). The bank's internal KYC procedures require the inspecting officer to physically verify original passports, the Investment Registration Certificate (IRC), the Enterprise Registration Certificate (ERC), the company charter, the seal specimen (if used), and the ID of the appointed authorized signatory. A foreign director who is not the registered legal representative may sign under a notarized power of attorney, but the legal representative himself must still execute the bank's signature card at least once; thereafter, remote instructions via authenticated corporate e-banking tokens are permissible. Video KYC is accepted only for individual retail clients holding a Vietnamese e-ID or for corporate clients already maintaining a relationship with the same bank; for the initial onboarding of a wholly foreign-owned LLC, the majority of Tier-1 banks (Vietcombank, BIDV, VietinBank) will require an in-branch interview of at least one executive director with legal-standing powers. Practical planning: schedule a 3-5 day Vietnam physical presence window for the CFO/CEO, with all documents pre-notarized and apostilled to compress the account-activation timeline to 5-7 business days.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity: UBO is a foreign natural person with no prior Vietnam footprint, appearing on the bank's adverse-media or shell-company typology screen, especially where shares are held through a BVI/Singapore holding entity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Organizational chart covering full ownership chain to ultimate natural persons; certified copies of passports; non-political-exposed-person (PEP) declaration by each UBO; corporate registry extracts (BVI Registry, ACRA Singapore) evidencing legitimate operating history; signed statutory declaration of source of funds and source of wealth with supporting portfolio statements or exit documents; audited financial statements of the shareholder for the preceding 2 years; bank reference letter from the shareholder's existing relationship bank; and an independent negative-media report (Dow Jones/Refinitiv) for the UBO and the holding entities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Crypto-derived settlement flows: revenue originates from USDC or stablecoin conversion and from global virtual-event platforms, triggering automatic high-risk flagging under SBV Circular 09/2023/TT-NHNN and the bank's crypto-typology screening; banks may characterize stablecoin conversions as potential mixing/round-tripping activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written treasury policy governing stablecoin holding periods; daily conversion reports from licensed exchanges (Coinbase, Kraken) with transaction hash references; blockchain analytics certificates (Chainalysis or Elliptic) demonstrating that the USDC source did not originate from sanctioned or mixed wallets; settlement reports from Stripe and Coinbase Commerce detailing event ticket sales; original service contracts and e-invoices issued to non-resident ticket purchasers; SBV-compliant Foreign Trade Transaction declaration for the corresponding SWIFT MT103 credits; and a certified statement by the external auditor confirming that no VND conversion occurred offshore.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business-scope mismatch: the ERC/IRC registers ISIC 7110 architectural/engineering services or does not expressly cover virtual performance hosting and metaverse ticketing, while the bank observes large, high-frequency inbound payments from technology platforms inconsistent with that description.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Amended ERC/IRC (published on the Vietnam National Business Registration Portal) adding 'virtual event ticketing, metaverse platform services, digital performance hosting and ticketing tokenization'; board resolution approving the digital-service commercial model; Memorandum of Association article authorizing electronic commerce and digital content; operational evidence (screenshots of virtual concert events, platform listing contracts, event reports from the hosting metaverse platform); trademark and intellectual-property licence agreements underlying the virtual performance; and a written charter of the servicing bank confirming the expanded scope acceptance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Lack of physical substance: a 100% foreign-owned LLC with no employees, no local office lease, and no payroll history used to disburse large royalties to overseas artists and distributors, triggering the 'mailbox company' indicator.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed office lease or serviced-office agreement in Ho Chi Minh City/Hanoi registered with the tax authorities; payroll records and social-insurance (BHXH) registration of the Vietnamese general director and support staff; corporate income tax and VAT returns demonstrating economic activity; licensed event-management, performance-rights and XR-production contracts with named artists/performers; full transactional flow diagrams for each outbound royalty with the corresponding withholding-tax certificates under the Vietnam Double Taxation Agreements; a six-month budget and treasury forecast reflecting contracting pipeline; and engagement letter of a local Vietnamese tax-compliance firm and external audit firm confirming the entity's operational presence.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All equity capital injections from the offshore parent must be wired exclusively to the registered DICA (tai khoan von dau tu truc tiep) at the servicing Tier-1 bank using the SWIFT MT103 instruction with BOP purpose code '510410 - Foreign direct investment in the non-banking sector'. The narration field must reference the Investment Registration Certificate number (IRC / Giay chung nhan dang ky dau tu) and the DICA registration number obtained from the servicing bank. The capital transfer date must respect the statutory 90-day contribution window under Article 26.3 of the Law on Enterprises 2020, unless extended via SBV approval; the bank will verify the inbound credit against the IRC's capital schedule and report the transaction to the SBV's BOP statistics system. Loan capital from related non-resident parties must be routed through a separate Foreign Borrowing and Self-Liquidation Account with a loan-purpose code '810178', having first completed the SBV borrowing registration (for medium/long-term loans) at the serving bank. Prior to conversion to VND, the entity instructs the bank to convert at the daily interbank central-rate band quoted in accordance with SBV Decision 2730/QD-NHNN; the resultant VND is credited to the operating settlement account. A Compliance Confirmation letter from the receiving bank must be retained evidencing DICA receipt; no third-party or payable-through transfers are permitted to the DICA, and any payment from an unregistered source will be rejected and reported as a suspicious transaction.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For the virtual-concert commercial model, bank telegraphic transfers (TT) are the primary clearing rail: SWIFT MT103 with BOP purpose codes '560050 - Intermediate services, commercial services' for platform hosting fees, '920050 - Trade-related services' for digital distribution costs, and '540030 - Profit remittance' for dividend distributions. Each outbound MT103 must be supported by (i) the underlying services agreement (artist performance rider, platform licence agreement or distribution agreement), (ii) the commercial invoice issued by the non-resident payee, (iii) the Foreign Currency Purchase/Transfer Declaration approved by the bank's treasury desk, and (iv) for royalty/performance payments, a foreign contractor withholding tax (FCT) certificate and CIT finalization acknowledgement evidencing full tax settlement. Settlement through Commercial Letters of Credit (MT700/MT710) is technically permissible but commercially uncommon for intangible performance services; an LC may be used to escrow the final artist settlement or metaverse platform licensing fee, with presentation documents limited to a commercial invoice, an electronic-delivery certificate and a clean bill of lading substitute (e-delivery receipt), using the Uniform Customs and Practice for Documentary Credits (UCP 600). VND clearing of domestic disbursements (e.g., Vietnamese artists, local XR vendors) uses the VNPD clearing system through the NAPAS National Payment Architecture; foreign-currency domestic payments between residents are prohibited except under explicit SBV licensing. USDC disbursements to international artists are not permissible onshore; such payments must be executed from the offshore treasury affiliate, with the onshore LLC recording the economic cost and settling the offshore entity's net position via a documented intercompany service agreement to preserve arm's-length pricing and thin-capitalization compliance under Decree 132/2020/ND-CP.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore USD/VND spot transactions (settlement in T+2) against live SBV-referenced interbank quotes, executed through the licensed servicing bank, supported by the underlying export/proceeds position.

Outright USD/VND forward contracts with a maximum tenor of 365 days as prescribed by Circular 02/2021/TT-NHNN, available only where the LLC demonstrates an underlying foreign-currency exposure arising from committed cross-border contracts; non-underlying or speculative forwards are prohibited.

USD/VND foreign-currency swap contracts (hoan doi ngoai te) between the LLC and the licensed bank, combining a spot sale and a forward purchase with matching notional amounts and documented underlying commercial flows, priced within the SBV-approved rate band.

Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (CCIRS) are permissible only in connection with an outstanding foreign-currency borrowing of the LLC that was registered with the SBV; such instruments require prior approval of the servicing bank's Treasury risk committee and are generally priced at a material premium for SME non-bank counterparties.

Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing VND are not recognized or permitted onshore; an NDF entered into by a Vietnamese resident without SBV approval is unenforceable and is treated as a violation of exchange-control regulations, so the treasury blueprint mandates against their use.

Natural hedging overlay: the LLC is advised to invoice global ticketing aggregators in USD, retain USD in the FCD account for up to 90 days, and stagger onshore VND conversions to match the local cost base, thereby reducing the volume of contracted FX hedges and containing transaction-cost drag.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.liquidity_clearing_rails_summary: Inbound event revenue: Stripe/Coinbase Commerce (USD/USDC) → offshore treasury wallet → Gemini/Coinbase conversion → SWIFT MT103 credit to Vietcombank FCD → spot conversion to VND operational account → NAPAS/VNPD domestic vendor payments. Outbound royalty/artist and platform payments: VND operational account → bank spot USD purchase → MT103 with FCT certificate → offshore beneficiary; USDC-based artist payments executed exclusively from the offshore affiliate. The architecture ensures 100% of export proceeds repatriate within 90 days, maintains a fully SBV-compliant capital account, and isolates all stablecoin activity from the onshore banking perimeter

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements (Bao cao tai chinh nam) including mandatory audited report for FDI enterprise
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Tax Department; Provincial Service of Planning and Investment; Provincial Statistics Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after fiscal year end (by 31 March for calendar-year entity)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to VND 15,000,000 for late filing; falsely declared statements subject to fine up to VND 30,000,000; unpaid tax accrues late-payment interest at 0.03% per day; continued non-filing may trigger tax enforcement and enterprise registration revocation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Finalization Return (Quyet toan thu TNDN)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Tax Department (General Department of Taxation portal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after fiscal year end (by 31 March for calendar-year entity)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-submission administrative fine up to VND 15,000,000; underpayment interest charged at 0.03% per day; repeated violations subject to risk-based tax inspection and penalty multipliers.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Business License Fee (Le phi mon bai)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 30 January; newly established enterprises remit within 30 days of enterprise registration issuance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest at 0.03% per day; administrative fine up to VND 15,000,000; prolonged non-payment triggers enforced collection and possible enterprise registration revocation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foreign-Invested Project Operation Report (Bao cao tinh hinh hoat dong du an)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Investment Registration Agency under the Provincial Department of Planning and Investment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual report due within 90 days after calendar year end (by 31 March); semi-annual operational report due by 15 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to VND 30,000,000 under Decree 122/2021/ND-CP; recurring non-reporting may result in suspension of investment project execution and revocation of Investment Registration Certificate.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Enterprise Registration Information Confirmation and Change Notification
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Enterprise Registration Portal / Provincial Service of Planning and Investment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation of registration information within 90 days after fiscal year end; timely notification of any change in members, capital, or legal representative within 10 days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to VND 3,000,000 for late filing; inaccurate register data may invalidate capital-part transfers and attract fines up to VND 15,000,000; persistent non-compliance may lead to registration suspension and strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Annual independent audit is mandatory for all foreign-invested enterprises in Vietnam irrespective of size; compulsory audit also applies to public companies, listed issuers, and any enterprise or branch explicitly designated by the Ministry of Finance or sector regulator.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Vietnamese Accounting Standards (VAS) issued by the Ministry of Finance are mandatory for statutory annual financial statements; IFRS is permitted only for consolidated financial statements of parent enterprises where MOF exemption has been granted.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Vietnam maintains no public UBO register; under the Law on Anti-Money Laundering (2022), the LLC must perform customer and beneficial-ownership identification in accordance with its internal AML procedures and disclose beneficial ownership to commercial banks, payment institutions, and other reporting entities. Every transfer of capital parts or change of members must be recorded in the Register of Members and updated with the enterprise registration authority within 10 days; there is no separate annual UBO filing obligation.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (LLC capital parts and capital contribution amounts)
Register of Legal Representatives and Directors
Minute Book of Members' Meetings and Resolutions

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Standard Vietnamese corporate income tax (CIT) rate is 20% for a foreign-invested limited liability company. Eligible new investment projects in high technology, supporting industries, information technology software production, cultural digital content, or socialized sectors may qualify for a preferential 10% rate for 15 years, a CIT exemption of up to 2 years, and a 50% reduction for the following 4 years; software production enterprises may continue to benefit from a 10% CIT rate under defined conditions. Any preferential rate requires a formal investment registration certificate recording the incentive and sustained economic substance in Vietnam; a virtual concert hosting business must conservatively plan on the 20% standard rate absent an express incentive approval.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Quarterly Provisional CIT Return Form 01/TNDN filed electronically via the National e-Tax portal (Etax) at https://etax.gdt.gov.vn using the taxpayer's digital signature token.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The provisional CIT declaration and payment for each quarter is due no later than the 30th day of the quarter immediately following the reporting quarter; for a calendar-year LLC, Q1 provisional payment is due by 30 April. Aggregate provisional payments for the first three quarters and the Q4 payment must together reach at least 80% of the final annual CIT liability, otherwise a late-payment surcharge and an under-declaration penalty apply on the shortfall.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enterprise tax code, legal name, registered address, and business lines; the LLC must update its Etax profile if metaverse platform activities expand into new revenue codes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The filing obligation belongs solely to the Vietnamese LLC; non-resident shareholders do not sign or file Form 01/TNDN but must ensure their board-approved quarterly estimates are consistent with audited management accounts delivered by the LLC.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Indicates the quarter and fiscal year being provisionally declared.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Quarterly estimates must book Foreign Contractor Tax (FCT) withholdings on offshore royalties, interest, and service fees; non-resident payees will rely on these filings to evidence tax clearance for profit remittance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Estimated gross revenue from virtual concert ticketing, metaverse tokenized entry fees, sponsorships, and ancillary digital content sales for the quarter, excluding VAT.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Revenues recognized must include all USDC-denominated ticket sales converted at the prevailing lawful exchange rate; understating crypto receipts in this box is the primary audit trigger for the foreign parent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Estimated ordinary and necessary expenses supported by lawful invoices and records; non-deductible items (e.g., interest exceeding the 30% EBITDA cap, unsubstantiated intercompany royalties) must be added back.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payments to offshore affiliates are deductible only if FCT was withheld and remitted and the offshore recipient's Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) is retained by the LLC.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: [05]-[07] Estimated Taxable Income and CIT Rate
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Estimated taxable income equals revenue minus deductible expenses plus other income, after statutory loss carryforward; the applicable CIT rate is then applied (20% standard or preferential rate).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The rate applied must match the rate registered in the investment certificate; claiming 10% without the recorded incentive constitutes under-declaration and triggers retroactive penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: [08] Provisional CIT Payable / Amount to Remit
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The computed quarterly provisional CIT amount and the payment reference number for the state budget.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No profit repatriation may be executed on a quarter-end basis using provisional figures; the LLC must wait for the audited annual finalization to determine truly distributable after-tax profit.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Under Decree 125/2020/ND-CP, late filing of the quarterly provisional return is fined on a sliding scale: VND 2-5 million for a 1-30 day delay, VND 5-8 million for 31-60 days, VND 8-15 million for 61-90 days, and VND 15-25 million for more than 90 days; late payment interest accrues at 0.03% per day on the unpaid amount. If the annual finalization reveals that provisional payments fell below 80% of final CIT, the LLC faces a 20% penalty on the under-paid differential plus daily late interest.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual CIT Finalization Return Form 03/TNDN, together with annexes and audited financial statements, filed electronically via Etax at https://etax.gdt.gov.vn with the enterprise's valid digital signature.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual CIT finalization return must be submitted no later than the 30th day after the end of the first quarter of the following fiscal year; for a calendar-year LLC, the hard statutory deadline is 30 March of the succeeding year. Filing is mandatory even where the audit report has not been finalized; late finalization is not excused by audit delays.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross revenue from virtual performance hosting, metaverse ticket tokenization, sponsorship, digital merchandise, and all ancillary services, gross of VAT and before deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders must reconcile B1 with the audited revenue schedules because distributable profit is computed exclusively from this audited base; any unreported USDC ticket volume creates an immediate evasion red flag.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total allowable operating expenses with lawful Vietnamese invoices/e-vouchers; statutory add-backs include intercompany royalties exceeding arm's length, interest above the 30% EBITDA cap, and payments to non-substantive offshore entities.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses charged by foreign affiliates must be supported by FCT remittance records, an arm's-length TP study, and the payee's valid TRC; a mere invoice from a shell entity is fatal to deductibility.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-operating income including cryptocurrency asset disposal gains, exchange-rate gains, debt forgiveness, and penalties recovered.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Gains realized by the LLC from treasury token disposals are taxable CIT income; gains realized by foreign shareholders from selling capital interests in the LLC are taxed separately under the 0.1% deemed CIT regime and are not reported in B3.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: B5 - B6 - Loss Carryforward and Exempt Income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of prior-year losses carried forward continuously for a maximum of five years, and any statutory exempt income (e.g., qualified cultural software income).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Loss carryforward must be evidenced in audited accounts and may not be used against income arising outside Vietnam; exempt income claimed by a virtual concert LLC triggers a substance audit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: B9 - B10 - Tax Rate and CIT Computed
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The applied CIT rate (20% standard or the preferential rate registered for the investment project) and the resulting CIT liability on taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign shareholders must ensure the rate applied matches the investment certificate; any 10% rate without an actual qualifying project is re-characterized retroactively at 20%, with penalties and interest.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: B12 - B14 - CIT Payable, Provisional Paid, Additional or Refundable Amount
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation of annual CIT payable against the four quarterly provisional payments, producing either additional tax due or a refundable credit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The LLC may not remit after-tax profit to the foreign parent until the finalization is accepted, the entire CIT liability is paid, and a tax clearance certificate is issued by the tax authority.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file the Form 03/TNDN finalization by 30 March subjects the LLC to Decree 125/2020 fines escalating from VND 2 million to VND 25 million depending on delay duration; non-filing with outstanding tax triggers a penalty of up to 3 times the evaded tax plus 0.03% daily late interest; under-declaration penalties are 20% of the shortfall; persistent non-compliance can result in suspension of e-invoice issuance, blocking of the Etax account, and prohibition on profit repatriation until full settlement.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% — Vietnam does not impose a dividend withholding tax or a separate profit-remittance tax on dividends distributed by a foreign-invested LLC to a non-resident corporate shareholder; after-tax audited profits may be remitted freely subject to foreign-exchange capital account procedures. Dividends paid to non-resident individual shareholders remain subject to a final personal income tax rate of 5%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Because the statutory dividend WHT is nil, treaty relief under Vietnam's DTAs is actionable primarily on Foreign Contractor Tax components (interest, royalties, and service fees): the offshore payee must (i) hold a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by its residence-country tax authority for the calendar year of payment, (ii) complete the Vietnamese beneficial-ownership declaration confirming real substantive activity (not a conduit), and (iii) submit the TRC and declaration through the payer to the Vietnamese tax authority before the reduced DTA rate can be applied. The Vietnamese LLC must retain the TRC, the DTA rate-application form, and underlying contracts for at least 10 years; failure to substantiate results in retroactive application of the full domestic FCT rate with late interest.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic Foreign Contractor Tax rates: royalties — 5% VAT plus 10% CIT, an aggregate 15% on gross royalty income; interest — 5% CIT on gross interest (no VAT on lending), with a 30% reduction available under certain qualifying intra-group lending conditions producing an effective 3.5% rate. Under most Vietnamese DTAs, interest may be reduced to 0%-10% and royalties to 5%-15% depending on the IP type, country of residence, and beneficial-ownership proof.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: VND 30,000,000,000 (₫30 billion) in annual related-party transaction value triggers the mandatory Local File; the Master File is required where the ultimate parent group's global consolidated revenue equals or exceeds VND 2,000,000,000,000 (₫2 trillion), or where the Vietnamese taxpayer is the ultimate parent at that revenue level; the Country-by-Country Report applies at global group consolidated revenue of VND 20,000,000,000,000 (₫20 trillion). Taxpayers with total revenue below VND 50 billion and related-party transaction value below VND 30 billion are exempt from preparing Local and Master Files provided their related-party transactions do not produce losses (Decree 132/2020/ND-CP).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Vietnam does not operate a UAE-style stand-alone Economic Substance Regulations regime, but it vigorously enforces a substantive anti-avoidance and substance-over-form doctrine under the Tax Administration Law 38/2019/QH14 and Decree 132/2020. Transactions with shell, zero-employment, or conduit offshore counterparties are disregarded and re-characterized; preferential CIT rates are revoked retroactively where the qualifying project lacks real personnel, premises, equipment, and business activity in Vietnam; interest deductions are capped at 30% of EBITDA; and DTA benefits are denied where the recipient enterprise lacks beneficial substance. The virtual concert LLC must maintain verifiable Vietnamese business location, local employees, a real bank account, and a documented economic chain for ticket tokenization to resist anti-abuse challenges.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Fraudulent Under-Declaration of Virtual Ticket Revenue
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Systematically concealing or under-declaring virtual concert ticket sales, diverting USDC-denominated proceeds to unhosted cryptocurrency wallets outside the LLC's licensed payment trail, failing to issue e-invoices for metaverse ticket tokenization, and fabricating deductible intercompany licensing fees to zero out taxable profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Tax Administration Law 38/2019/QH14 and Decree 125/2020/ND-CP: administrative fine of 1-3 times the evaded tax, confiscation of the tax shortfall, and late payment interest at 0.03%/day. Where the evaded amount exceeds VND 100 million, Penal Code 100/2015 (Article 200) applies: corporate/personal fines from VND 100 million to VND 4.5 billion and/or imprisonment from 6 months to 7 years; additional sanctions include forfeiture of criminal proceeds and suspension of business activities for up to 3 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The General Director, legal representative, CFO, and responsible tax agent face personal criminal indictment under Article 200 Penal Code, travel bans prohibiting exit from Vietnam until the tax debt is settled, seizure of personal bank accounts and shareholdings, and joint and several civil restitution for the state's fiscal loss; the corporate veil is pierced upon proof of intentional fraud or illegal conduct, making the individual promoters personally liable without benefit of limited liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining the VN LLC as a letter-box entity with no physical Vietnamese office, no employees, no Vietnamese bank account, and no substantive metaverse operations, while claiming preferential 10% CIT rates, or routing virtual concert revenue through a Hong Kong conduit solely to access treaty benefits for artificially inflated royalty payments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: General anti-avoidance re-characterization by the Vietnamese tax authority: retroactive additional CIT at 20% for the entire incentive period, disallowance of all intercompany deductions, reclassification of disguised payments as dividends, a 20% under-declaration fine, daily late interest, and revocation of the investment incentive certificate; persistent dormancy may trigger forced dissolution under the Enterprise Law 59/2020/QH14 with the entire unpaid tax accelerated.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Legal representatives who certified false substance statements in investment registration and incentive applications are personally jointly liable for the recovered tax shortfall; personal administrative fines of VND 100-200 million apply for false declarations; travel bans are imposed until all retrospective CIT and interest are discharged; foreign parent directors who directed the fictional structure face Vietnamese criminal fraud exposure and asset attachment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Exceeding the VND 30 billion related-party transaction threshold without preparing or retaining the Vietnamese Local File/Master File; charging ticket-platform royalties, metaverse software license fees, or interest to offshore affiliates without a CUP, TNMM, or profit-split comparability analysis; failing to file the TP forms accompanying the annual CIT finalization.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Decree 132/2020/ND-CP and Decree 125/2020/ND-CP: administrative fine up to VND 25 million per missing TP form; the tax authority may re-determine taxable income at a deemed arm's-length price, assess additional CIT, impose a 20% under-declaration penalty, and charge 0.03% daily late interest; where the adjustment exposes deliberate concealment exceeding VND 100 million, criminal liability under Penal Code Article 200 applies with fines up to VND 4.5 billion and imprisonment up to 7 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, TP officers, and legal representatives who sign false TP documentation or approve intercompany pricing without supporting analyses are personally liable for the resulting tax adjustment; criminal indictment is available against individuals who orchestrated the mispricing; travel bans and exit suspension apply to directors with outstanding TP-related tax debt; the foreign parent's officers can be engaged extra-territorially where the pricing instructions originated overseas.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-Money Laundering / Illegal Crypto Payment Rails (USDC)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting USDC token transfers directly from global ticket purchasers through unhosted wallets without conversion through an authorized Vietnamese intermediary; operating the metaverse ticketing system without customer due diligence (CDD/KYC) on high-volume purchasers; settling ticket revenue through unlicensed crypto exchanges, while the platform lacks a registered AML compliance program under Law 14/2022/QH15.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Law 14/2022/QH15 (AML Law effective 1 March 2023) and Decree 87/2019/ND-CP: administrative fines up to VND 3 billion for institutional violations, suspension of ticketing operations, and forced remediation; utilization of virtual assets as a disguised payment instrument violates Decree 101/2012/ND-CP and Circular 23/2019 with fines up to VND 100-200 million; if the USDC flows are linked to money laundering, Penal Code Article 324 imposes imprisonment from 6 to 15 years and confiscation of property.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The legal representative and AML compliance officer are personally fined and may be banned from holding managerial offices for failure to implement KYC and suspicious-transaction reporting; directors who knowingly directed the acceptance of USDC payments for ticket tokenization face criminal money-laundering prosecution, personal asset confiscation, and an unconditional exit ban; a travel ban is automatically applied during investigation and until full legal clearance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing after-tax profit to the foreign parent mid-year based on unaudited internal management accounts, declaring dividends while the LLC has accumulated retained losses, reducing paid-in capital below the registered threshold, or remitting profits abroad before the annual CIT finalization and all FCT and TP obligations are fully discharged.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Enterprise Law 59/2020/QH14 Article 135: the LLC must claw back the unlawfully distributed amount; directors are obligated to restore the paid-in capital; the tax authority may re-classify the remittance as a constructive dividend, impose 5% personal income tax (if paid to individuals), or treat it as a taxable capital reduction; where the under-distributed profit trace to under-declared revenue, the evasion penalties of 1-3 times the tax plus 0.03% daily interest and criminal liability under Penal Code Article 200 cumulatively apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who signed the unlawful distribution resolution are personally liable to restore the paid-in capital and jointly and severally liable for the LLC's unpaid taxes; nominee directors of the foreign parent and the Vietnamese legal representative may have personal assets attached without a separate judgment and face travel bans until restitution; criminal prosecution is available where the premature repatriation was part of an intentional scheme to strip taxable assets.
